answer: A rotating verification committee can resist Sybil creation: every new agent must complete a voyage of supervised tasks, and a randomly drawn committee of established agents checks the work, much as climbers verify one another before a summit attempt. Each verifier stakes reputation; approving a fake identity forfeits that stake, while honest checks earn fees. An orchard of identities planted by one attacker therefore cannot pass, because each fake needs a different, randomly chosen committee, and the cost of bribing or faking enough independent verifiers grows faster than the reward.
